resource_measurement: CPU and memory are estimated by trapezoidal integration of Docker stats samples for all base and request-scoped containers matching the MCP target group. Integration starts at warmup start and ends at the detected cold-demand/supersession boundary or forced run cleanup. Overlapping discarded warmups for one group split that group's sampled integral equally. Samples are taken at the configured interval; attribution is estimated at group/container level, not directly measured per warmup process.
lifecycle_accounting: A started predictive executor counts as a warmup only if its executor created or resumed a container (effective=true). It is marked used when a later demand for the same MCP group reaches a running/resume ready state after that warmup started. A hit additionally requires the warmup to be ready before the demand activation began. Thus a late-but-used warmup is not counted as a false positive. Discard timestamps are detected boundaries, not directly observed Docker removal timestamps.
attribution_limitations: C1 prompt/stream prewarming is disabled in c2_only mode. In c1_c2 mode, if both mechanisms target the same MCP group, timing and group-level Docker stats cannot causally separate their contribution.
hit_rate_accounting: Eligible sandbox requests are tool_group_activation_requested events whose MCP group maps to a predictive-stage prewarm_schedule candidate in that run, including activations that did not reach a ready event. Candidate server aliases are mapped to runtime MCP group names. A hit requires an effective predictive executor and a running/resume ready event after the warmup started; a hit additionally requires the warmup to have completed before activation began.
aggregation: Hit and false-positive rates pool numerators and denominators across completed sessions. Per-session discarded counts and resource integrals are pooled totals divided by completed sessions. Resource means include zero-cost sessions with no discarded warmups; records missing sufficient Docker samples are counted separately.
